result.topic_en: Euler solves for the angle ω and the coefficients α, β, γ, δ in the equation for a simple vibration mode of an elastic lamina, showing that cos ω is always negative, and writes the resulting displacement formula.
result.transcription:
$\ast$ ) 135 ( $\ast$
cuius aequationis reſolutio praebet
$2 + (p-q)(e^{\omega} + e^{-\omega}) + pp + qq = 0$,
vnde ob
$pp + qq = 2$ et $p - q = 2\,\mathrm{cof.}\,\omega$ reperitur
$\mathrm{cof.}\,\omega = \frac{-2}{e^{\omega} + e^{-\omega}}$,
vnde patet Coſinum anguli $\omega$ ſemper fore negatiuum, ideoque angulum $\omega$ in quadrantibus ſecundo et tertio, item ſexto et ſeptimo, item decimo et vndecimo, etc. quaeri debere. Ex cognito autem coſinu $\omega$ concluditur vel
$\mathrm{fin.}\,\omega = \frac{e^{\omega} - e^{-\omega}}{e^{\omega} + e^{-\omega}}$, vel $\mathrm{fin.}\,\omega = \frac{-e^{\omega} + e^{-\omega}}{e^{\omega} + e^{-\omega}}$,
quos duos caſus ſollicite a ſe inuicem diſtingui oportet. At ex priore caſu colligitur:
$\frac{\alpha}{\beta} = \frac{1 - e^{-2\omega} + e^{\omega} - e^{-\omega}}{-1 + e^{2\omega} + e^{\omega} - e^{-\omega}} = \frac{1}{e^{\omega}}$;
ex altero autem valore ipſius $\mathrm{fin.}\,\omega$ colligitur $\frac{\alpha}{\beta} = -\frac{1}{e^{\omega}}$.
Rite igitur his caſibus combinandis impetrabimus ſequentes valores:
$\alpha = 1,\ \beta = \pm e^{\omega},\ \gamma = 1 \mp e^{\omega}$ et $\delta = 1 \pm e^{\omega}$,
quibus ſubſtitutis aequatio pro hoc motu ſimplici erit
$y = C\,\mathrm{fin.}\,(\zeta + t\sqrt{\tfrac{2g}{k}})$
$(e^{u\omega} \pm e^{\omega(1-u)} + (1 \mp e^{\omega})\,\mathrm{fin.}\,u\omega + (1 \pm e^{\omega})\,\mathrm{cof.}\,u\omega)$,
vbi, vt hactenus, denotat $u$ fractionem $\frac{s}{a}$, denique erit vt ante
$f = \frac{a}{\omega}$, $k = \frac{a^4}{bcc\,\omega^4}$, $\sqrt{\frac{2g}{k}} = \frac{\omega\omega c\sqrt{2gb}}{aa}$,
tempus

items.quote: vnde patet Coſinum anguli $\omega$ ſemper fore negatiuum, ideoque angulum $\omega$ in quadrantibus ſecundo et tertio, item ſexto et ſeptimo, item decimo et vndecimo, etc. quaeri debere.
items.english: whence it is clear that the cosine of the angle ω will always be negative, and hence the angle ω must be sought in the second and third quadrants, likewise the sixth and seventh, likewise the tenth and eleventh, etc.

items.quote: quos duos caſus ſollicite a ſe inuicem diſtingui oportet.
items.english: these two cases must be carefully distinguished from each other.
